_comment: MeshGrammar substrate — rule-based procedural mesh generation. Each recipe defines a seed shape, grammar rules, and generation count. The MeshGrammarNode applies rules to reshape topology. Use #recipe:<name> or named variants.

mesh_grammar.name: MeshGrammar Substrate
mesh_grammar.description: Universal mesh grammar substrate. Start from a seed shape, apply rule-based operations (extrude, inset, split, branch, scatter) across generations. The only substrate where the algorithm reshapes topology itself.
mesh_grammar.qfep_connection: Rules do not decorate the seed, they rewrite its topology — each generation appended to a scrubbable history, with a max_faces ceiling as the only thing between grammar and runaway growth. Form as sentence: parse it again and the object is a different object.

mesh_grammar_seed.name: MeshGrammar — Seed Icosahedron
mesh_grammar_seed.description: Raw icosahedron seed — no rules applied. The starting point for all mesh grammar forms. 20 triangular faces, uniform topology.
mesh_grammar_seed.qfep_connection: Twenty identical triangles and no rules applied — the grammar's silence made solid. Every other form in the family is this icosahedron plus a sentence, which makes the unrewritten seed the invariant against which all rewriting can be felt.

mesh_grammar_extruded_spire.name: MeshGrammar — Extruded Spire
mesh_grammar_extruded_spire.description: Two-stage extrusion on upward faces — pushes faces outward and scales them down, creating a spire. Demonstrates extrude operation and tag-based chaining.
mesh_grammar_extruded_spire.qfep_connection: Two extrusions, the second addressed only to tag:extruded_top — the spire exists because one rule can speak to the output of another. Height as grammar's compound interest, narrowing from scale 0.7 to 0.6 as it climbs.

mesh_grammar_inset_pattern.name: MeshGrammar — Inset Pattern
mesh_grammar_inset_pattern.description: Inset operation on all faces — shrinks each face toward its center, creating a lattice of gaps. Pure topological subdivision.
mesh_grammar_inset_pattern.qfep_connection: Every face shrinks 0.35 toward its own center and a lattice arrives as the negative space between retreats. F_order made of withdrawal: pattern is what remains when each unit pulls back from its neighbors.

mesh_grammar_subdivided.name: MeshGrammar — Subdivided Sphere
mesh_grammar_subdivided.description: Midpoint subdivision on all faces — each triangle splits into four. The icosahedron approaches a sphere. Demonstrates split operation.
mesh_grammar_subdivided.qfep_connection: Split turns one triangle into four without adding a single decision — resolution rises while the rule stays one line. Roundness arrives as a limit of repetition: the sphere as what an icosahedron keeps almost becoming.

mesh_grammar_nodule_sphere.name: MeshGrammar — Nodule Sphere
mesh_grammar_nodule_sphere.description: Random bulge on sphere faces — sparse bumps with ring depth and smoothing. Organic ceramic-like surface.
mesh_grammar_nodule_sphere.qfep_connection: Each random bulge drags two rings of neighbors with it, half-smoothed — a bump here is never private, because continuity taxes every swelling. 'Organic' names exactly this: deformation that cannot happen to one face alone.

mesh_grammar_coral_fingers.name: MeshGrammar — Coral Fingers
mesh_grammar_coral_fingers.description: Tube branches growing from upward-facing random faces — curved, segmented fingers reaching outward. Demonstrates tube_branch operation.
mesh_grammar_coral_fingers.qfep_connection: Fingers grow only from upward-facing faces, chosen at random — orientation is destiny, chance picks the individuals. Reaching coded as a class privilege of 'up': the sphere's underside never gets to want anything.

mesh_grammar_crumpled.name: MeshGrammar — Crumpled Form
mesh_grammar_crumpled.description: Noise displacement on upward faces — Perlin noise pushes vertices along normals. Crumpled, weathered ceramic surface.
mesh_grammar_crumpled.qfep_connection: One Perlin pass along the normals and the pristine sphere reads as weathered ceramic — entropy applied as a single reversible rule. Damage without history: the crumple is E_flux's costume, worn by a mesh nothing ever touched.

mesh_grammar_budding.name: MeshGrammar — Budding Sphere
mesh_grammar_budding.description: Extrude random faces then delete the tops — creates hollow buds and openings. Demonstrates extrude + delete composition.
mesh_grammar_budding.qfep_connection: Growth and wounding compose: every bud is an extrusion that lost its cap, so the hollowness of the form is exactly the record of what the second rule removed.

mesh_grammar_branching_coral.name: MeshGrammar — Branching Coral
mesh_grammar_branching_coral.description: Multi-generation tube branching — first generation grows branches, second generation branches from branch tips. Recursive growth from tag chaining.
mesh_grammar_branching_coral.qfep_connection: Growth recurses through naming: each tube leaves a branch_tip tag and the next rule grows only where the last one signed. Coral as a bureaucracy of addresses — no global plan, just tips filing for extension.

mesh_grammar_inset_towers.name: MeshGrammar — Inset Towers
mesh_grammar_inset_towers.description: Inset upward faces then extrude the inset — creates architectural towers rising from a cube. Order of operations matters.
mesh_grammar_inset_towers.qfep_connection: Inset carves the plots, extrude raises blocks from tag:inset — swap the two operations and no towers appear. The whole architecture lives in sequencing: the city on the cube is a non-commutative sentence.

mesh_grammar_detailed_bulge.name: MeshGrammar — Detailed Bulge
mesh_grammar_detailed_bulge.description: Split all faces first to increase resolution, then apply sparse random bulges — fine-grained organic detail from subdivision + deformation.
mesh_grammar_detailed_bulge.qfep_connection: Subdivision comes first because twenty coarse faces cannot hold a wound — resolution must be purchased before deformation can register. The mesh has to be made sensitive before anything can happen to it.

mesh_grammar_noise_sculpture.name: MeshGrammar — Noise Sculpture
mesh_grammar_noise_sculpture.description: Cellular noise displacement on all faces — radial deformation creates alien, geode-like surfaces. Different noise type than Crumpled Form.
mesh_grammar_noise_sculpture.qfep_connection: Every vertex consults a cellular noise field at its own coordinate and moves radially by what it hears — no vertex sees the field whole, yet the geode reads as one intention. Coherence is a property of the field, not of any negotiation among the parts.

mesh_grammar_petal_flower.name: MeshGrammar — Petal Flower
mesh_grammar_petal_flower.description: Petal splay on upward faces — radiating curved petals with tilt and curl. Organic decoration operation.
mesh_grammar_petal_flower.qfep_connection: The selector is the politics: only faces whose normals point up are granted petals, so the bloom records an orientation privilege before it records any botany. Each petal is an open strip with quadratic curl — ornament the closed mesh never promised, surface without volume.

mesh_grammar_scale_armor.name: MeshGrammar — Scale Armor
mesh_grammar_scale_armor.description: Subdivide then apply overlapping pointed scale tiles — armadillo-like surface. Split increases resolution, scale_tile adds decorative geometry.
mesh_grammar_scale_armor.qfep_connection: Split first, then hand every face the same tilted scale — armor not as design but as redundancy, protection assembled from one rule repeated past counting. The overlap parameter is the treaty: each scale covers part of its neighbor's base, so no single tile ever answers alone for the body underneath.

mesh_grammar_riveted.name: MeshGrammar — Riveted Sphere
mesh_grammar_riveted.description: Extrude random faces, delete tops to create openings, then place edge beads along boundaries — industrial aesthetic from three composed operations.
mesh_grammar_riveted.qfep_connection: Industry is three verbs deep: extrude, delete, bead. The rivets are not fasteners but a rule that decorates every wound the deletion left open.

mesh_grammar_barnacle.name: MeshGrammar — Barnacle Sphere
mesh_grammar_barnacle.description: Surface scatter operation — randomly placed small spheres across the mesh surface. Density and size range control the colony appearance.
mesh_grammar_barnacle.qfep_connection: Scatter adds tenants without renovating the building — small spheres settle on faces at density 0.3 while the host mesh keeps its topology untouched. Colony as surface condition: living on someone else's structure, in geometry.

mesh_grammar_lsystem_tree.name: MeshGrammar — L-System Tree
mesh_grammar_lsystem_tree.description: L-system branching from upward faces — fractal tree growth using turtle interpretation. Bush preset with configurable angle and generations.
mesh_grammar_lsystem_tree.qfep_connection: A string grammar rides inside the mesh grammar: a bush axiom is rewritten twice, then a turtle walks the sentence into tubes, capped at 30 branches. The tree is literally a text — its shape is what an alphabet does when given a body.

mesh_grammar_ca_growth.name: MeshGrammar — CA Growth
mesh_grammar_ca_growth.description: Cellular automata on mesh faces — coral rule tags faces alive/dead, then alive faces extrude. Algorithm reshapes topology based on neighbor counting.
mesh_grammar_ca_growth.qfep_connection: A coral-rule automaton runs four steps over the face graph, then only tag:ca_alive faces earn extrusion — the relief is a census of neighborhoods. Seeded at 42, the growth replays identically: emergence with a receipt.

mesh_grammar_spike_ball.name: MeshGrammar — Spike Ball
mesh_grammar_spike_ball.description: Dense normal-aligned spike scatter — aggressive radial geometry from surface scatter with spike shape and high density.
mesh_grammar_spike_ball.qfep_connection: Each face flips a weighted coin — density as probability — and the winners grow a normal-aligned spike at a point the RNG picks by barycentric lottery. Menace as sampled distribution: reseed and the bristling redistributes, same statistics, different spikes.

mesh_grammar_blooming_bulge.name: MeshGrammar — Blooming Bulge
mesh_grammar_blooming_bulge.description: Sparse random bulges followed by petal splay on bulge tips — organic compound form where deformation creates the anchor points for decoration.
mesh_grammar_blooming_bulge.qfep_connection: First the swelling, then petals splayed only on tag:bulge_tip — ornament can grow only where deformation has already marked an address. Blooming staged as consequence, not decoration.
